steps: Agree with your analytics team the page and block events to measure, and list what your current tracking already captures so nothing is counted twice.
Add tracking for the agreed events to your Edge Delivery pages and blocks, using your existing consent controls, Web SDK and datastream.
Test with consent given, refused and not yet answered, then trace sample events to the dataset and your CJA data view.
deliverables: Event list for pages and blocks
Page and block events on your Edge Delivery pages
Test results for consent and for sample events
asks: Your consent controls, Web SDK, event schema, datastream, dataset, CJA connection and data view already in place
An analytics contact to agree the events and check them in CJA
Permission to add tracking to your Edge Delivery pages
risk: Interactions collected without a visitor's consent: we send the new events only when your existing consent controls allow it, and test each consent case before sign-off.
outcome: The agreed page and block interactions on your Edge Delivery pages reach your CJA data view, collected according to each visitor's consent.

steps: Agree with your review leads at which step of your Frame.io reviews the brand validation results are read, and by whom.
Agree with your review leads what happens to an asset that fails before sign-off, and write both decisions into a one-page review guide.
Try the agreed steps on one real review in Frame.io with your review leads, and adjust the guide from what the trial shows.
deliverables: Agreed review step for brand validation results
One-page guide for assets that fail
Trial on one real Frame.io review
asks: Review leads who can agree how your reviews run in Frame.io for Business
One real review in Frame.io to try the agreed steps on
risk: Assets signed off before anyone reads the brand results: we set the review step where they are read, and try it on one real review first.
outcome: Your reviewers read the brand validation results in Frame.io at an agreed step of each review, with an agreed path for assets that fail before sign-off.

steps: Agree with your production lead which production workflows have their outputs validated against your brand guidelines, and the volume each one runs at.
Estimate the Operations the brand checks use at the planned volume, from each Skill's consumption rate in the Rate Card, and share the estimate with your production lead.
Run a test batch through one workflow and check that the validation results reach your reviewers in Frame.io for review and sign-off.
Agree with your production lead which failed outputs are rerun before review, and record that rule for each workflow.
deliverables: List of workflows whose outputs are checked
Operations estimate at the planned volume
Test batch with results in Frame.io
Rerun rule for failed outputs
asks: A production lead who knows your workflows and their planned volumes
The Rate Card for the Operations you license, with each Skill's consumption rate
Reviewers with access to Frame.io to look at the test results
risk: Brand checks using more Operations than you planned for: we estimate them at your planned volume and test on one batch before the checks go wider.
outcome: Outputs of the production workflows you choose are validated automatically against your brand guidelines, with results in Frame.io for review and sign-off and an agreed rerun rule.

steps: Train your designers to run the Adobe Brand Intelligence plugin in Figma: choose the context, such as channel, audience and product data, and set the number of variants.
Review what the plugin assembles with your designers on a real campaign, adjusting single assets or regenerating with other assembly options, starting with two or three variants.
Agree with your designers and review leads how finished variants go on to review, and write it into a one-page guide for the team.
deliverables: Training for designers on the Figma plugin
Practice variants reviewed with your designers
One-page guide to sending variants to review
asks: Designers with access to the Adobe Brand Intelligence plugin in Figma
Your prepared Figma templates, with contexts and assembly options already configured for your brand
A real campaign your designers can practice on
risk: Variants that miss what the campaign needs: we train designers to review each result against it, adjust single assets or regenerate, before the agreed hand-off to review.
outcome: Your designers create on-brand variants in Figma with the Adobe Brand Intelligence plugin, review and adjust them, and send finished variants to review the agreed way.

steps: Agree with your team the pilot users and the AI platform for Coworker: one you already use, from Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini Enterprise or Databricks Genie One.
Help your platform administrators approve and deploy Coworker for the pilot users, following Adobe's setup steps for that platform.
Test prompts from your own work with each pilot user under their own Adobe permissions, and show your team what Coworker answers there and what stays in the Coworker interface.
deliverables: Coworker approved and deployed for your pilot users
Tested prompt set
Short guide to what Coworker answers in the platform
asks: Your administrators for the AI platform, to approve and deploy Coworker
Pilot users with Coworker access in Adobe and access to the platform
Questions your team asks every week, to turn into test prompts
risk: Users expecting the full Coworker interface in their AI platform: our guide shows that answers there are read-only insights and what stays in the Coworker interface.
outcome: Your pilot users ask Coworker questions in the AI platform they already use and get answers that match the data they can see in their Adobe applications.

steps: Agree with your Fusion administrator whether Coworker connects with a service account or a personal account, since Coworker can change whatever that account can.
Build the agreed scenario around Run a Prompt and Get Execution Status, with its trigger, a prompt mapped from earlier modules, and the storage and follow-on modules it needs.
Route results that need input or approval to a person, save Task IDs for long tasks, and set error handling that never resends a prompt whose outcome is uncertain.
Test the scenario on real cases with your process owner, checking that each completed run did its business action, since a completed status does not guarantee it.
deliverables: Coworker connection in Workfront Fusion on the agreed account
Tested scenario around Run a Prompt and Get Execution Status
Routing for results that need input or approval
Test record of real cases and their business actions
asks: A decision on the account Coworker connects with, and its access
Access to Workfront Fusion and the systems the scenario reads and writes
A process owner to agree the scenario and check test results
risk: Changes beyond what you intended: the modules cannot restrict individual tools, so Coworker connects with an account whose access you choose, and approvals go to a person.
outcome: A tested Fusion scenario sends prompts to Coworker on the agreed trigger and uses its answers, routing anything that needs input or approval to a person.
